subject: Evening: Streaming chat throughput regression during peak - customer escalation
messages:
From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finexa.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 19:03:12 -0500
Subject: Re: (URGENT) Evening spike — streaming chat p99 blowup

Monica —

We started seeing a large jump in 99th-percentile latency on your hosted streaming chat endpoint around 18:42 local. Users on our live support channel are experiencing long stalls and disconnects; throughput dropped 40% while error rate climbed. Attached a short tcpdump and our client logs. This is hitting us at peak support hours.

Immediate ask: can Redwood route our traffic off the streaming cluster or flip us to a non-streaming fallback while you investigate? We need a mitigation ASAP — this is affecting our SLAs.

Thanks,
Mike Turner
Head of Ops, Finexa
attachments: finexa-client-logs-20261118.zip, client-trace.txt
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finexa.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 19:10:45 -0500
Subject: Re: (URGENT) Evening spike — streaming chat p99 blowup

Hi Mike — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're seeing the same signal on our monitoring. I'm escalating to infra/serving and product immediately.

Quick responses and next steps:
- I've asked engineering (cc'ed) to look for recent config changes and autoscale gaps.
- Can you confirm whether you're using SSE or the websocket path for these sessions? (We saw mixed client patterns which matters for routing.)
- Temporary mitigation: we can flip your routing to the non-streaming /v1/chat/generate (polling) endpoint for the duration of the incident; it will increase token cost but should restore request completion. Do you want us to proceed?

We'll provide a timeline within 30 minutes. Sorry for the disruption — we know this is high impact.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — customer escalation lead
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 19:25:08 -0500
Subject: Re: (URGENT) Evening spike — streaming chat p99 blowup

Monica / Lauren — initial triage notes from the serving runtime: 
- Symptom: sudden p95/p99 latency uptick and connection stalls concentrated on SSE connections served by cluster pool 'stream-east-7' starting ~18:40. Websocket traffic shows a smaller but noticeable tail.
- Root signals: increase in per-request KV-cache miss rates and a queue backlog on the prefix-batching worker. The runtime's continuous batching piles up during bursty short requests and then underfits batch sizes, causing extreme tail latency.
- Autoscale: group 'stream-east-7' hit min->max spin-up but the scale-up lag is ~70s (we saw recent smaller scale limits from yesterday's policy tweak).
- Correlation: a spike of many concurrent short chat prompts from Finexa's org (1000+ concurrent ephemeral sessions) matches the timing.

Immediate mitigations I can apply now (low risk):
1) Increase autoscale max replicas for stream-east-7 (instant trigger) and temporarily lower scale-up CPU threshold to accelerate spin-up.
2) Enable short-circuit fallback for SSE connections so long-running blockers get closed and client can reconnect to polling endpoint.
3) Reduce maximum batch latency (ms) to force smaller, faster batches for short prompts.
4) Route Finexa to the dedicated lightweight streaming pool (if capacity available) or to polling endpoint as Monica suggested.

I'll attach the trace dump we pulled from the worker and a condensed flame capture. Also filing INF-9876 on JIRA.

--Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Site Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: sse-trace-logs-20261118.txt
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: (URGENT) Evening spike — streaming chat p99 blowup

Team — thanks Sean. Quick product notes and proposed customer communications: 
- Short plan (60 minute window): 1) Apply autoscale policy change and reduced batch latency (Sean). 2) If p99 doesn't fall to baseline within 15m post-change, route Finexa to polling endpoint and open a dedicated capacity slot for them (Monica to coordinate). 3) Post-incident: deep root-cause + perf regression analysis and tighten canary on any changes to scale thresholds.
- External comms: propose we offer Finexa a 20% credit for the hour of impact and a postmortem within 72 hours. Rafael — need approval to offer the credit and to prioritize capacity for Finexa tomorrow morning.

I'll prepare a short exec note and the update for the customer.

Lauren Bishop
Product Lead — Streaming & Runtime, Redwood Inference

-Rafael

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finexa.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 21:07:45 -0500
Subject: Action update: streaming regression and mitigation steps (Finexa)

Mike — quick update and immediate actions taken: 
- At 19:30 we applied an autoscale policy adjustment for stream-east-7 and lowered batch latency; monitoring showed initial improvement.
- At 19:35 we enabled SSE short-circuit fallback and began routing new Finexa sessions to the polling endpoint. This restored completion for ~95% of requests; throughput back to expected levels by 19:42.
- Our incident JIRA INF-9876 contains traces and the change set; postmortem scheduled within 72 hours.

Per earlier note from our product team, we will apply a one-time 20% credit for the impacted hour (authorized). We'll also prioritize a dedicated capacity slot for you tomorrow morning to avoid recurrence during your peak.

Apologies again for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority and will follow up with the root-cause writeup and permanent mitigation plan. If you want us to keep you on polling for a longer window while we confirm stability, say the word and we'll keep the route in place.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
